issues.note: The since-clause needs the past simple: since I last saw him.
Since when is a real idiom, but it may belong to since-adv or since-prep.
The wrong correction contradicts the adaptation note; it also flags the example clash.
The note says past simple main clause, but its illustration uses present perfect has been.
The correction must be the present perfect: I have lived here.
A duplicate link is a small redundancy; the compare note itself is useful.

findings.F1: The sense 1 example uses the present perfect in the since-clause (since I have last seen him).
findings.F2: The learner-error correction 'I am living here since I was ten' is still wrong and contradicts the adaptation note.
findings.F3: The sense 2 semantic adaptation note's rule (main clause in past simple) does not match its own illustration (has been).
